penalties_applied.name: requires_human_fulfillment
penalties_applied.reason: Any viable solution — whether a workaround guide, a consulting engagement, or a deployment automation script — requires per-customer human judgment to assess the specific org configuration, namespace structure, and Salesforce DX setup. There is no one-size-fits-all automated delivery here.

penalties_applied.name: requires_synchronous_human
penalties_applied.reason: Salesforce ISV clients expect scoping calls, onboarding discussions, and live troubleshooting — especially given the complexity of Salesforce packaging environments. A pure async self-serve product is implausible in this ecosystem.

rationale: The pain is real and commercially severe — blocked AppExchange revenue directly affects ISV livelihoods — and the buyer (Salesforce AppExchange partner with a developer license) is a named business role with clear budget authority. However, the nature of the problem makes automation-first delivery essentially impossible: diagnosing and working around Salesforce namespace packaging bugs requires hands-on access to specific org configurations, and every engagement would demand a sales/scoping call and custom per-customer work. Operational_autonomy scores 3 and buildability_with_ai scores 4, both well below their build_gate floors, and the heavy human-fulfillment and synchronous penalties drop the total to 3.5. This is a legitimate consulting opportunity, not a factory-compatible product.
solution_plan: The underlying opportunity is real: Salesforce ISV developers are blocked from shipping AI features and are actively searching for a fix. A consulting or 'done-for-you' workaround service could charge $500-2000 per engagement to audit a partner's namespace configuration and implement whatever manual bypass Salesforce's known-issue status allows. The factory could draft an outreach email to AppExchange partners (found via Salesforce AppExchange directory or LinkedIn) and a landing page describing the service — Youval approves the send. BUT: every delivery requires Youval (or a hired Salesforce developer) to do real hands-on Salesforce DX work per client. This is not a product the factory can run autonomously; it is a freelance consultancy that the factory can help market. A non-technical solo operator cannot fulfil this without a Salesforce expert, so the honest recommendation is to drop unless Youval has or can hire that expertise — and even then, it is time-bounded to the period before Salesforce patches the known issue.
notes: operational_autonomy (3) and buildability_with_ai (4) both fail their build_gate floors (7 and 6 respectively). requires_human_fulfillment and requires_synchronous_human penalties applied. The opportunity is real but fundamentally a high-touch consulting play, incompatible with the factory's autonomy requirements. Also time-limited: Salesforce will likely patch this within 1-3 release cycles.
